Slide 1: Intro

Gladiator Advicelol, Grandmaster Advicelol. Top 0.001% in some of the most competitive online games of all time; This was my identity. Matthew didn’t exist. I dissociated myself from reality and escaped into the digital realm. The real me was trapped inside my mind fighting a continuous battle against depression, anxiety, and an inability to control my attention. I struggled to socialize, to speak, to make decisions, and I was insecure about my appearance. To top it all off school was a slow paced recurring nightmare of boredom that failed to keep me engaged and motivated enough to reach my potential.

Games knew how to keep me engaged, how to keep me focused, keep me playing, and motivate me to be the best I could be toward the goal that they wanted. I loved games. They taught me to be growth oriented. They help me core aspects of who I am. This alone was enough to keep me me to pushing forward.
